items.abstract_or_text: # v0.32.0 ## Highlights This release features 814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)! * **Structured decisions and generic parsers**: the new `POST /v1/systemone` endpoint answers `choice`, `noul` and `score` questions over a structured state (#59299), is served by default (#60677, #60696), and also runs on `Cloudflare/clef-omni` (#61064), `LiquidAI/d1-3B` (#60676) and DiffusionGemma (#60466). The new `hf` tool and reasoning parser (`--tool-call-parser hf`, `--reasoning-parser hf`) reads the checkpoint's `response_template`, so models that ship it need no model-specific parser (#58604, #58602), in both the Python and Rust frontends (#59005). * **Low-precision KV cache everywhere**: NVFP4 KV cache now runs on SM8x and SM12x (#46963), SM90 (#60620) and with XQA decode on SM12x (#60452), and on MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on SM100 (#59300); GLM-5.x defaults to an FP8 KV cache on SM100, halving KV memory per rank with 2.3-5.5% more throughput at a 7-11% TTFT cost in the PR's benchmark (#60140, #60281); `fp8_ds_mla` on SM90 gives GLM-5.3-Flash up to 31% more output throughput (#59246); ROCm gains the 4-bit `ultraquant_4bit` KV cache with about 2x the density of FP8 (#57057). * **Model Runner V2**: a GPU n-gram speculator with variable-length drafts (#40704), Elastic EP (#53934), pipeline parallelism with prefill context parallelism for MLA models (#59139), a stock torch.compile mode (#59079), and MRV2 is now the default on ROCm with the model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360). * **Faster startup and serving**: `vllm download-kernels` installs FlashInfer's precompiled kernels (#58765); `vllm preload --preload-autotune` keeps the FlashInfer autotune table warm across restarts (#60085); a shared-memory tensor arena broadcasts large multimodal tensors to workers with one copy (#51207); tokenizers and processors load from the local snapshot (#60825); and with `--api-server-count` above 1 each connection goes to the least-loaded API worker, for 43-85% more req/s on short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, 32 input / 1 output tokens) in the PR's benchmark (#60723). * **Model support**: new EmbeddingGemma 2 omni-modal embeddings (#60254), MiniCPM-V 4.7 (#58674) and Nemotron 3.5 ASR (#59827); video input in the Transformers modeling backend (#57441); GLM-5.3 sparse MLA index conversions reused across layers (3.5-3.9x on that kernel, #59464) and fused multi-step draft decode (13.3% at concurrency 1, #57443); HiSparse per-request residency caching for up to 58% more throughput on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200 with long, fully GPU-resident contexts at high concurrency (#60083). * **Security**: fixes for GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7 (chat template resource exhaustion, #50300), GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4 (tokenizer `max_token_id`, #59491) and GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9 (P2P ZMQ socket exhaustion, #51504); CORS no longer allows every origin by default (#61009); untrusted images are limited to raster formats (#60022); shared-memory multimodal cache handles are signed (#59357); and JSON schemas nested deeper than 64 levels are rejected (#60036). * **Breaking changes**: Python 3.10 dropped (#60402); default CORS origins restricted (#61009); `transformers>=5.16.1, =0.23.2` (#57387, #59796); torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes removed (#60517); cascade attention removed (#61126); `mamba_cache_mode="all"` removed (#58997); `max_tokens` no longer reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API reasoning stream events renamed (#59652). ## Release Artifacts ### Python Wheels | Platform | Install | |---|---| | PyPI (CUDA 13.0) | `pip install vllm` | | PyPI (CUDA 13.0, uv) | `uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto` | | ROCm | `pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.32.0/rocm723` | | XPU | `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/0.32.0/xpu --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu --index-strategy unsafe-best-match` | ### Docker Images | Platform | Docker Image | |---|---| | CUDA 13.0 (Default) | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0` | | CUDA 12.9 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0-cu129` | | CUDA 13.0 + Ubuntu 24.04 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0-ubuntu2404` | | CUDA 12.9 + Ubuntu 24.04 | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0-cu129-ubuntu2404` | | ROCm | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0` | | CPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.32.0` | | XPU | `docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.32.0` | ### Other Artifacts Pre-built release artifacts are available in the **Assets** section at the bottom of this page, including: - Source distribution tarball - CUDA 12.9 Python wheels for x86_64 and arm64 - CUDA 13.0 Python wheels for x86_64 and arm64 - CPU Python wheels for x86_64, arm64, and macOS - XPU Python wheel for x86_64 ## Model Support * **New models**: EmbeddingGemma 2 (`google/embeddinggemma-2`), an omni-modal text/image/audio/video embedding model, with unused modality encoders skipped through `--limit-mm-per-prompt` (#60254, #60289); MiniCPM-V 4.7 (#58674); Nemotron 3.5 ASR (`nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b`) complete-audio transcription; native realtime streaming is not yet supported (#59827); `Cloudflare/clef-omni` (#61064) and `LiquidAI/d1-3B` (#60676) on `/v1/systemone`; PLaMo 3 reasoning and tool parsers (#56575); and the zerank-2 reranker score template (#60415). * **Transformers modeling backend**: video inputs (#57441), and Glm, Arcee, CWM, Mellum (#59679), GPT-NeoX, Phi, Seed-OSS and Jais2 (#59701) now served through it. * **New model capabilities**: LoRA for BERT, RoBERTa and XLM-RoBERTa embedding models (#61033); Granite as an EAGLE3/DFlash target (#60855); Qwen3-ASR EAGLE3 (#52824); Sarvam MLA EAGLE3/DSpark with PP (#55902); GLM-5.3-Flash with the DFlash2 drafter (#56983); and MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 at PP > 1 on MRV2 (#57197) with MTP sharing target embeddings under PP (#58648). * **GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash**: sparse MLA index conversion reused across layers (#59464), fused multi-step draft decode (#57443), FP8 KV cache default on SM100 (#60140, #60281), `fp8_ds_mla` on SM90 (#59246), qlnorm skipped for MHA (4.4-7.7% TTFT, #58845), long-context indexer prefill sharded across TP (up to 25% lower TTFT at 1M context, #54951), DCP for the kpool indexer (#59211, #60032), KDA prefill checkpoints with FlashKDA (#56960), FP8 KV on SM90 sparse MLA (#55222), `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` honored for KDA state (#59147), a generic packed KV layout (#57169), MTP index sharing restored (#61079), and fixes for vision-tower crashes (#59126), non-square image encoder budgets (#59565), DP startup (#56974), video timestamps (#55647), DFlash2/EAGLE3 aux hidden states (#60763) and null-block writes (#59528). * **DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1**: decoder-side SWA bounded replay (#58132) with replay layers in CUDA graphs and trimmed in PIECEWISE graphs (`compilation_config.decoder_replay_trim_threshold`, #59532) plus last KV-source layer trimming (+3.6%, #59894), packed FP8 Engram exchange across DP (#59923), faster CPU-offloaded Engram lookups (#59327), fused DeepSeek V4 + MTP drafting (#58463), encoder CUDA graph packing for V4.1 and Kimi-K3 (11% lower mean TTFT, #58925), EPLB for DSpark drafts (#57549), and fixes for NVFP4 checkpoints with 0% draft acceptance (#59655), MegaMoE shared-expert finalize ordering (#59927), worst-case vision dummy inputs (#57898, #59271), compressor ring null-block writes (#58560), Triton 3.9 indexer quantization (#60716) and decoder-replay CUDA graphs with FlashInfer EP MoE backends (#61041). * **Qwen**: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp) merged QSA projections in one GEMM (1.45-1.68x, #59533), fused QSA pre-indexer (#57097), sequence parallelism through `--enable-hc-sp` (#56322), SM100 low-latency decode GEMM plans (up to 2.7x vs cuBLAS on small-M, #59214), `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` honored (#60023), and PLE loading for INC (#59990), Quark (#59443) and pre-SM89 GPUs (#60142); Qwen3-VL/Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 M-RoPE cache 4x smaller and Qwen3.5 YaRN matching Transformers (#59853); Qwen3-Omni M-RoPE fixes (#58890, #59842); Qwen3-ASR on the upstream processor (#57146); Qwen3-VL unknown video fps (#60501) and per-video options with the multimodal cache (#55203). * **Kimi-K3 and MiniMax-M3**: Kimi-K3 FlashInfer fused speculative KDA on SM100 (#54255), fused vision processor (10-20x preprocessing at 1080p-8K, #59278), fused K/V pack on the DCP prefill path (#56881), and DSpark KV cache back to 4 groups (#59733); MiniMax-M3 MSA prefill with an E4M3 query (26-37% faster with FP8 KV, #60684), FP8 indexer cache on non-SM100 GPUs (#59081), Triton indexer tuning (#56151, #59481), and indexer score fixes (#60194, #54597). * **Multimodal**: device-side input normalization for Qwen3-VL/Qwen3.5/Qwen4Exp (#51289), GLM-V and GLM-OCR (#55389), Llama Nemotron VL (#57928) and Kimi K2.5/K3 (#59278), kept fused under `compile_mm_encoder` (#59195); encoder inputs sorted by modality (6.5-8.2% more req/s, #60196); Mistral 3 preprocessing 8% faster (#57531); Pixtral `compile_mm_encoder` (#57168); and fixes for Llama 4 / Mistral Large 3 EAGLE drafters (regression since v0.28.0, #57633), Phi-4 MM audio OOM (#60614), DeepSeek-OCR zero-sum pixels (#59417), MiMo-V2.5/V2.6 with fastsafetensors (#58142), MiMo-V2.6 FP8 KV cache (#58128), Voxtral realtime (#45022), Nemotron Super vision LayerNorm (#61401), K-EXAONE config and MTP RoPE (#60187), Nemotron Parse tied `lm_head` (#60272), LongCat-Flash MTP loading (#60080) and Ling-3.0-flash-VL (#59026). ## Engine Core * **Model Runner V2**: GPU n-gram speculator (#40704), Elastic EP with drain-then-commit scaling (#53934), PP with PCP for MLA models (#59139), `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE` mode (#59079), dynamic K in autoregressive speculators (#57053), MTP sampling-mask replay (#59359) and per-module LM heads (#58921), non-blocking H2D copies on WSL2 (#60215), and fixes for int64 index offsets at long context (#60736), warmup (#61013), GDN prefill checkpoints (#59536) and MRV2+PP+MTP align state (#60210). * **Speculative decoding**: fused multi-step draft decode on FlashInfer trtllm-gen (#58371), FlashInfer ReplaySSM for Mamba2 MTP (#52928), in-graph metadata for DFlash/DSpark drafts (#60692), and correctness fixes for ngram on hybrid recurrent models (#56531), Mamba prefill checkpoints with MTP and prefix caching (#59759, #60797), stop-string trimming (#47616), draft model config (#61240), adaptive block verification (#60945), DSpark bonus slots (#59105) and draft models on the Transformers backend (#59293). * **Hybrid models and prefix caching**: Mamba2 internal prefill checkpoints for NemotronH, Granite-4.0-H, Falcon-H1 and Zamba2 (#57329), stale block hashes dropped when streaming sessions truncate (#59103), and fixes for quantized Mamba-2 with TP (#58083), spec decode page sizes (#59975), prefix-cache bounds (#55601, #60533) and sm90 Mamba2 NaNs (#61718). * **Sleep and RL**: sleep releases workspace scratch (up to 4.5 GiB/GPU, #59156) and KV-init state (about 4.6 GiB/GPU, #59158), opt-in `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` (#59160, #59523); token-level weight-version spans on outputs (#59582, #61070); weight-transfer communicators released without stopping inference (#61060); `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names 'draft.*'` (#61046); `modelexpress` weight-transfer backend (#58399); `POST /weight_checker` (#51350); weight-transfer metrics (#55781); `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` releasing the MNNVL workspace (#59360); and `sleep(level=2)` keeping FP8 KV scales (#57163). * **HiSparse**: per-request residency cache (up to 58% at high concurrency with GPU-resident contexts, #60083), lower scheduler overhead (#57930), GPU residency owned by HiSparse (#60647), less staging memory (#60429), host cache gauges (#58949, #59485), and fixes for decode token limits (#60682) and TP hangs (#60941). * **Startup and memory**: shared-memory tensor arena (`--enable-shm-tensor-arena`, on by default, #51207), Fast Start with PP (#55477), daemon-held weights counted against `gpu_memory_utilization` (#57298), autotune preload (#60085), local tokenizer snapshots (#60825), `sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor` saving several GiB at 1M context (#61023), cached memory reclaimed during weight loading (#57516), fewer Triton sampler warmup compiles (#58605), sharded state loader with PP (#52110), and `reload_weights` with Run:ai streamer (#58124). * **Kernels and runtime**: MoE weighted-sum tuning (1.17-2.37x, #59731), flash-maxsim kernels for ColBERT/ColPali scoring (#40337), fallback detokenization with 69% less CPU at 32K tokens (#60497), faster KV block free queue (#60269), Triton kernels off `tl.make_block_ptr` (#60502), fusion passes restored under PyTorch 2.15 (#57299) and static FP8 quant fusion on recent torch (#61108). * **Batch invariance**: custom all-reduce under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (#58623), deterministic split-K LoRA shrink (#59377), every attention backend checked (#60271), SM120 TP configs (#58495), and ROCm support (#52231). * **Observability**: `vllm:prompt_tokens_cached_by_source_total` (#56318), `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage` (#58874), `vllm:admission_rejections_total` (#55812), `vllm:watermark_requests` (#58715), `--custom-histogram-buckets` (#48867), a JSON log formatter via `LoggingConfig.formatter` (#58739), and per-session profiling controls (#57875). ## Large Scale Serving * **MoE communication**: FlashInfer CuteDSL MegaMoE for more models via `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` (#54049), FP8 combine for the FlashInfer one-sided all2all (+4% at DEP8, #57995), NCCL symmetric-memory MoE reduce-scatter (9.6-16% lower latency, #49194), DeepEPv2 hybrid NVLink+RDMA mode on by default (#57991), Kimi-K3 shared experts with DeepEP v2 (#56875), and opt-in EPLB migration batching (#52641). * **Context parallelism**: decode requests sharded across PCP ranks (#52162) and TokenSpeed MLA with block-interleaved DCP for heterogeneous NIXL disaggregation (#59462). * **KV connectors**: NIXL host-buffer copies coalesced (#54483), mixed block sizes (#58860), peer metadata recovery (#55471) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MTP acceptance in P/D (#59997); Mooncake coalesced hybrid/MLA RDMA regions (#57952) and bootstrap retries (#55923); MoRIIO Kimi-K3 DSpark READ (#57700); DeepSeek-V4.1 P/D skipping bounded replay for loaded KV (#59197); and KVCR pool-and-index API (#59899). * **Data parallelism**: streaming requests pinned to their engine (#59017), per-engine RNG streams (#59788), and placement groups without `ray[default]` (#57648). ## Hardware & Performance * **NVIDIA**: native 64-head FlashMLA sparse prefill on SM100 (1.16-1.18x TTFT, #60029), block-FP8 DeepGEMM experts skipping padding (#59128), SM120 split-K attention (#58482), DGX Spark Qwen4Exp GEMM plans (#59753, #59632, #60027), OAI Triton MXFP4 MoE on SM12x (#58877), and FlashInfer autotune cache per rank (#57635). * **AMD ROCm**: DeepSeek-V4 AITER MegaMoEV2 via `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` (#59685) with opt-in shared-expert fusion (3-8%, #61004), opt-in mono decode for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X (`VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`, #60397), opt-in Gluon sparse MLA (up to +16% on GLM-5.2, #53492), paged MXFP4 indexer (#58671), opt-in a4w4 MoE for DSv4 (#58819), `ultraquant_4bit` KV cache (#57057), `aiter_flydsl` GDN prefill (#57560), Kimi-K3 prefill checkpoints (about 20% better TTFT, #58344), fused MLA decode (#57640) and per-rank latent MoE shards (#59591), GLM-5.3-Flash split-K sparse MLA decode (5-15% lower ITL, #58584), native `merge_attn_states` (2.4x, #60159), `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` for RDNA (#59132), gfx11 W4A16 tuning (up to 23% TTFT, #56301), MRV2 default with model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360), and fixes for sleep-mode segfaults on ROCm 7.2+ (#60367) and MLA weight reloads (#60389). * **Intel XPU**: MLA in `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` (#58297), Arc Pro B70 FP8 GEMM (2.0-2.73x, #56063) and fused MoE configs (#53065), fused SYCL LayerNorm (#57172), and fixes for Gemma-2 softcap (#58936) and DP+EP MoE (#57787). * **CPU**: vectorized sampler (up to 58x on s390x, #53913), aarch64 causal conv1d (about 9%, #54093), POWER10 AWQ/GPTQ (#59149), and PowerPC `dtype=auto` choosing bfloat16 (#58528). * **Other**: tpu-inference v0.31.0 (#60190) and out-of-tree platforms registering multiple attention backends (#41091). ## Quantization * **New capabilities**: online re-quantization of linear layers (`--quantization-config.linear fp8_per_channel`, #55684), per-token NVFP4 CuTe-DSL MoE (#50030) with ReLU2 (#56740), MXFP4 MoE oracle with CUTLASS W4A4 and BF16 fallback (#60079), compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE with FP8 activations (#59815), ModelOpt IQ2_XS/IQ2_XXS/Q8_0 on SM120/SM121 (#59604), `int4_per_token_head` KV with non-power-of-two heads (#56198), and Humming preferred over Marlin on SM90 (#56997). * **Fixes**: silent CUTLASS NVFP4/MXFP4 MoE corruption under EP (#59042), GPTQ with non-default safetensors names (#60411), `moe_wna16` 8-bit asymmetric zero points (#58950), and ModelOpt mixed-precision NVFP4 detection (#56050). ## API & Frontend * **New endpoints and options**: `/v1/systemone` (#59299, #60677, #60696), `hf` parser (#58604), `vllm download-kernels` (#58765), `output_mode: "text"` and `stop_reason` in `/inference/v1/generate` (#58588, #60251), `mm_payload` for render requests (#61427, #60728), Responses `min_p` and `stop_token_ids` (#48084, #56592), `LLM.chat(priority=...)` (#57243), and `/generative_scoring` `cache_salt` (#60841). * **Behavior**: `max_tokens` is an upper bound instead of a reservation, so long prompts are no longer rejected (#57035); least-loaded API worker selection (#60723); tool parser compatibility checked at startup (#59749). * **Tool calling and structured output**: `parallel_tool_calls=false` enforced (#50502, #59298), `tool_choice="required"` streaming (#60354) and native XML parsers (#47512), Step-3.5 and `minimax_m3` on the parser engine (#59321, #59743), xgrammar `propertyNames` (#57594), and LoRA PEFT `rank_pattern`/`alpha_pattern` applied with unsupported features rejected (#59801, #60225). * **Rust frontend**: `--grpc-port` (#59659), `--stream-interval` (#60589), `logprob_token_ids` (#59549), `Control.Shutdown` with `vllm-proto` 0.5.0 (#59316), `qwen3_json` parser (#60136), and Kimi K3 grammar fixes (#59190, #59395). ## Security * GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7: chat templates are validated statically and rendered under a timeout (`VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT`), user-supplied `chat_template` in Responses `chat_template_kwargs` is rejected, and the Rust frontend caps template execution (#50300). * GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4: tokenizer `max_token_id` off-by-one fixed (#59491). * GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9: P2P ZMQ peer sessions are bounded by `VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS` (default 128), `VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S` (default 30) and `VLLM_P2P_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` (default 300), so unique peer addresses can no longer exhaust ZMQ sockets (#51504). * Default CORS settings no longer allow every origin in the Python and Rust frontends; set `--allowed-origins` to permit browser origins (#61009). * Untrusted images are opened with a raster-format allowlist (`ALLOWED_IMAGE_FORMATS`), denying EPS/PostScript and WMF (#60022); shared-memory multimodal cache handles are HMAC-signed and forged handles rejected (#59357). * Structured-output JSON schemas nested more than 64 levels return 400 (#60036); chunked `/v1/embeddings` requests keep `cache_salt` (#47696); Phi-4 MM audio no longer holds multi-GiB attention matrices (#60614); DeepSeek-OCR zero-sum pixel tensors no longer kill EngineCore (#59417). * Security dependency bumps: `aiohttp>=3.14.3`, `pillow>=12.3.0`, cryptography, urllib3, pyjwt and others (#59249, #59315, #59427). ## Dependencies * `transformers>=5.16.1, =0.23.2` (#59796). * NIXL 1.5.0 (#56907), CuTe DSL 4.8.0 block-scale APIs (#59480), `humming-kernels==0.1.17` with initial Rubin support (#61556, #61858), InstantTensor 0.2.2 (#61167), and `flashinfer-jit-cache` excluded from wheel `install_requires` (#60052). * ROCm: AITER 0.1.24.post1 (#59794) and MoRI v1.2.3.post1 (#56073). XPU: auto-round-lib 0.16.0 (#60976). TPU: tpu-inference v0.31.0 (#60190). ## Build * Python 3.11-3.14 supported (#60402); macOS wheels built with the stable ABI (#60312); CUDA source builds require GCC 13 and fail early otherwise (#60259); Docker images compile Python bytecode at build time for faster container startup (#55422); `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED` finds a compatible published wheel within the last 20 commits (#58871); the vendored DeepGEMM uses `TORCH_LIBRARY` (abi3, #48962). ## Breaking Changes & Deprecations * Python 3.10 is no longer supported; the minimum is Python 3.11 (#60402). * Default CORS origins changed from `*` to none; set `--allowed-origins` for browser clients (#61009). * `transformers>=5.16.1, =0.23.2` are required (#57387, #59796). * The torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes were removed, along with `PassConfig.enable_sp`, `fuse_gemm_comms` and `sp_min_token_num`; model-level sequence parallelism is unaffected (#60517). * Cascade attention was removed; `--disable-cascade-attn` still parses but only warns and will be removed in v0.33.0 (#61126). * `mamba_cache_mode="all"` was removed; `--mamba-cache-mode all` now fails validation (#58997). * Previously deprecated APIs were removed: `wait_for_inflight_requests` (use `mode="wait"`), `AsyncLLM.pause_generation()`, `IOProcessor.output_to_response`, `vllm.scripts.main()` and `vllm bench throughput --dataset` (#60923). The `sonnet` benchmark dataset was removed as scheduled (#60129). Tensorizer support was removed from LoRA (#60024), and the PyO3 `vllm._rust_tool_parser` bridge was removed (#59744). * API changes: `max_tokens` is treated as an upper bound on output rather than reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API streaming uses `response.content_part.added/done` with `part.type="reasoning_text"` instead of `response.reasoning_part.added/done` (#59652); `SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_token_ids` is per row (#56984); `/inference/v1/generate` logprobs use integer token IDs (#58181); sleep API responses are standardized and invalid levels return 400 (#52864); `return_mm_kwargs` is deprecated in favor of `mm_payload` (#61427). * Watermarking: when the engine has watermarking configured, an omitted request field means enabled and only `false` opts out; unsupported combinations warn and fall back (#56801). * Rust frontend: `qwen3_xml` now parses Qwen3-Coder XML (alias of `qwen3_coder`); use the new `qwen3_json` for the JSON format (#60136). * New defaults: shared-memory tensor arena on (#51207); GLM-5.x FP8 KV cache on SM100 with `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (#60140, #60281); `VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_ALLOW_HYBRID_MODE=1` (#57991); Humming preferred over Marlin on SM90 (#56997); `sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor` 2 above 256K `max_model_len` (#61023); MRV2 on ROCm with model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360); `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=auto` (#59965); `dtype=auto` picks bfloat16 on PowerPC (#58528); MXFP4 W4A4 checkpoints fall back to W4A16 with a warning when no W4A4 kernel exists (#60079). * Stricter validation: incompatible `--prefix-match-unit` (#58021), `max_num_scheduled_tokens=0` (#60714), HiSparse with `cudagraph_mode=FULL` (#59688), and negative `--device-ids` (#49053) are rejected at startup. ## New Contributors * @0xViking made their first contribution in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60053 * @1fanwang made their first contribution in items.abstract_or_text: ui : Discover & Download Models from HF Hub (#29584) * common : resolve - download tags and list cached sidecars A Q4_0-mtp style tag now resolves the sidecar file when no model file matches it, so a solo draft or mmproj download actually pulls the file. Cached sidecar files list as their own entries so the state survives a restart, and removing such a tag deletes only the sidecar. Assisted-by: pi:zai-org/GLM-5.3 * ui : optional sanitized raw HTML in markdown Add an allowHtml prop to MarkdownContent: raw HTML found in the markdown is rendered after DOMPurify sanitization instead of being escaped as literal text. Default stays escaped. Assisted-by: pi:GLM-5.3-Flash * ui : add the discover models components The Discover surface: the curated-catalog list with its search and skeletons, the details pane with its readme, metadata, Hub stats and download options, and the standalone download progress bar that replaces the plain one. The quant download button sizes its select with a new xs trigger, so the select gains that size and the muted box look. The store stays incomplete when a repo fails, so the next mount retries it. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : put the discover view in the models manager The manager dialog gains its second view: the Discover Models call to action fades the table out, slides the title with its compass mark, and fades the discover surface in; the arrow button returns to the table. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash # Conflicts: # tools/ui/src/lib/components/ui/button/button.svelte * ui : add the Enable Discover Models setting The flag gates browsing and downloading HuggingFace GGUF models, so it is declared on the discover layer; the repo-tree lookup in the manager layer above reads it from here. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : resume model downloads from the pause point A stopped download keeps its partial file instead of deleting it, so re-posting the tag resumes from disk. The first progress record now carries the resume offset, the paused snapshot survives into the resumed entry, and a pause settles as soon as it is requested. Assisted-by: pi * ui : lead the discover list with downloads The discover sidebar lists running downloads above the suggested models, and steps aside while a query is active. A paused download stays in the manager table, where it is resumed or dropped. Assisted-by: pi * ui : make resuming a paused download work Re-posting the tag of a paused download hit the router's "already exists" check, because a paused download parks its entry as DOWNLOADED until the next reload: a download entry that is not running is now replaced and resumed. The UI keeps the paused row when the request still fails, instead of dropping it and looking finished. Assisted-by: pi * ui : remember unfinished model downloads A partial file is named after its content hash, so nothing on disk says which model it belongs to once the router restarts. The router now keeps the tags of the downloads it started, clears a tag when the download finishes or is deleted, and lists what is left as still downloading without starting anything. The UI adopts those tags as paused on every list fetch, so a refresh or a fresh open shows an incomplete download and can resume it from the files already on disk. Assisted-by: pi * ui : show a paused download's state on its chip A paused quant chip reads as paused at rest, the way a running one shows its spinner, and offers the resume action on hover. The selector's download row gets a View in Discover action beside its cancel. Assisted-by: pi * ui : collapse the download options by default The copyable download command starts collapsed so the option rows lead; expanding it stays one click away. Assisted-by: pi * ui : keep decision models out of the hub lists Decision models answer with calibrated probabilities instead of text, so llama-ui cannot run them: the hub data layer drops them from the catalog and every search, keyed by the decision-model tag or a text-classification pipeline. Assisted-by: pi * ui : read download tags as quant and sidecar A ` : - ` tag now parses into its quant and sidecar instead of one opaque quant token, and ModelsService.draftSidecarsByRepo collects the router listing's sidecar-only entries per repo, replacing the inline copy in the models store. Assisted-by: pi * ui : cluster draft downloads under their main model Tracked downloads group by repo: the main weights lead and the draft sidecars ride inside their item as compact sub-lines, on the selector, the discover list and the manager table. The main model's controls pause, resume and cancel the whole cluster, and the manager's download rows select into the configuration pane. Assisted-by: pi * ui : act on tracked downloads from the table rows The table passes its clusters' draft sub-lines to the model rows. A row's actions cascade pause and resume, an in-flight row offers Cancel download while a paused one keeps Delete from disk, and the confirm dialog's copy follows the state. Assisted-by: pi * ui : give downloads a configuration pane of their own Selecting a tracked download opens the pane in a download mode: live progress with pause, resume and cancel, and See in Discover, instead of metadata and load actions that a model without files cannot offer. Assisted-by: pi * ui : make the discover details self-fetching and responsive ModelsDiscoverDetailsContainer owns the details, tree and readme fetches so hosts outside the discover view can render the pane, and the details layout adapts to narrow panes with container queries instead of viewport breakpoints. Assisted-by: pi * ui : download a matching draft with the main model A main quant download now pulls the quant-matched draft of the most preferred kind the repo ships (DFlash before MTP), fire-and-forget, so speculative decoding is ready when the main lands. Manual draft chips stay available; the options row also collapses to one column in narrow panes. Assisted-by: pi * ui : keep discover off by default and couple it with the hub setting Discover Models starts unchecked. Enabling it turns the Hugging Face Hub setting on and disabling it turns it back off, so the checkbox never lies; with discover off the hub setting stays available on its own for the display data. Stored and reset state are corrected the same way on load. Assisted-by: pi * ui : open the manage models dialog on the manager view The dialog now opens on the manager instead of returning to the last view, discover entries still land on the discover view while the setting allows it, and the discover surfaces follow the setting's state. Assisted-by: pi * ui : give the discover search room for its focus ring The sticky search bar insets from the panel edges so the focus ring stays inside the scroll container, and rows scroll behind an opaque bar instead of through it. Assisted-by: pi * common: settle sidecar names on the listing and drop unfinished partials An infix or trailing sidecar token is ambiguous: draft heads use it (Model-MTP-BF16.gguf), so do full models with embedded heads (Model-Q8D-MTP.gguf). Such a name is a sidecar only next to token-free main weights of the same family, while mmproj or imatrix anywhere in the name, or a leading token, decides alone (mmproj_f16.gguf). A quant tag always carries its bit count, so a sidecar named after no quant (mtp-Model-it.gguf) gets the bare tag: the listing, the plan and remove all use it. An imatrix tag resolves into a plan slot of its own, downloaded but never wired into the params. remove resolves the tag the way a download does and deletes the partial files of every planned blob, so cancelling a running download or dropping one left unfinished by an earlier run leaves nothing on disk. The router passes its token and releases its lock around the call, and records the unfinished downloads with an atomic write. llama download succeeds on a sidecar-only plan and prints its paths. * ui : move dialog views and draft states into enums and constants The models dialog's views become the ModelsDialogView enum, the draft subline's states join ModelRowDownloadState, the view fade and the copy-feedback reset move to ui constants, and the dialog's compass marks come from DISCOVER_ICON. Assisted-by: pi * ui : drop the unused discover surface The dead openDiscoverModels twin, the commented-out command divider, the details pane's unused onClose and its header's close button, and a redundant type cast leave; the command's copy feedback joins the shared reset constant. Assisted-by: pi * ui : trim the download option comments and highlight the chat template The comment verbosity the options panel and its chips carried shrinks to the non-obvious why, and the chat template dialog renders through SyntaxHighlightedCode as jinja instead of a plain pre block. Assisted-by: pi * common: only a .gguf file is a sidecar, and mmproj/imatrix as whole words A non-GGUF file named like a sidecar (quantization-mmproj-Q8_0.json) is picked as the mmproj, and a sidecar word inside a longer word of a model name (Phi-2-OmniMatrix.i1-Q4_K_M.gguf) drops the model. * ui: dedupe draft sidecar badges per quant The draft sidecar badges deduped by kind and repo without the quant, so with a draft cached at two quants only one badge survived, and a delete of the other main quant found no badge to remove its sidecar with. Also restores the getDownloadEntries doc lost when the clusters method landed above it. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: adopt the incomplete download status and drop the paused-ids registry The store inferred an unfinished download from a downloading entry it held no local state for, which misread a download running in another tab as paused and offered a resume the server rejects. The listing carries the "incomplete" status now, so the adoption keys off it directly. The paused ids no longer need to survive in localStorage: the server remembers them across restarts, and the progress snapshot was stale after a reload anyway. The stale localStorage key is removed. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: quant-match the pause and cancel cascades Pause, resume and cancel cascaded to every draft sidecar of the repo while delete only took the quant-matched ones, so canceling a Q4_0 download also killed a Q8_0 draft that belongs to another quant's main. Every cascade acts on the quant-matched drafts now, matching what a delete takes with it. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: collapse the duplicated draft subline markup The downloaded and in-flight branches repeated the identical connector, label and badge markup; one block with a conditional tail keeps the two states in sync. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: scrub positioned styles out of sanitized model card html The style attribute stays allowed for the KaTeX output, which let a third party card draw a fixed overlay over the app. The sanitize hook drops position:fixed and position:absolute values and leaves the KaTeX layout styles alone. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: run the discover mount fetch once and reuse the shared repoOf helper fetch() toggles its loading flag synchronously inside the mount effect, which re-ran the fetch on every toggle and retried failed catalog repos endlessly; the effect now untracks the call. The local repoOf copy and the duplicate services import give way to the shared helpers. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: narrow the spec-type map to the draft sidecars SPEC_TYPE carried empty entries for the aux sidecars it is never indexed with; the map and the command component now type the badge as a draft sidecar through a draftBadgeOf helper instead of a cast. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: name the decision-model tags and markdown cache keys The decision-model hub tag and pipeline tag move into the huggingface constants next to the other pipeline tags, and the markdown transform cache prefixes get names instead of bare one-letter tokens. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: read the discover setting through one truthiness check Three places read the setting with !== false and one with Boolean(); all four read it the same way now. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * ui: compare the models dialog view against its enum The template compared the view state against the 'manage' literal in three spots while the script used the enum. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * nit: Remove `+` before draft sidecar badge * server: list unfinished downloads as incomplete A download that never finished was reported as "downloading", the same status a live download carries, so a client could not tell a running download from a dead one. The tags remembered in unfinished-downloads now list under a dedicated "incomplete" status, without an instance. Assisted-by: pi (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash) * server: download a model with its sidecars as -hf does Resolution goes back to master. POST /models takes the sidecar kinds to pull with the model (mmproj by default) and the download child gets them as -hf flags, so the server picks the files. /models lists real models only, each with the sidecars it has on disk, and incomplete downloads keep their sidecars across restarts. A stopped download keeps its partial files for the next attempt, and DELETE purges them through the same plan the download follows. * ui: download sidecars as parameters of their model The download options keep their chips, but a chip no longer posts a sidecar tag: the store maps it to its model and the sidecar kinds to pull, the quant chip takes its companion draft in the same download, and draft badges come from the sidecars each cached model lists. The server adds the sidecars a cached model lacks when it is posted again, and DELETE removes a single sidecar of a cached model. * ui : mirror the server's sidecar lookup in draft badges The server resolves a sidecar by the case-sensitive ` -` token in the same directory as the weights. The UI matched the token loosely, so a badge could offer a draft the server never pulls. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : post the model's sidecar kinds with its download The store keeps one download per model: the chip's kinds ride along with the model's own sidecars, and a download row no longer expands into one row per sidecar. Draft badges carry no quant of their own yet, so a sidecar of a cached model is never labelled with the model's quant. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : join a quant's draft into its download chip One chip per quant, its draft badged inside it and its size covering both files. The draft is the file the server would pick: the same directory, the exact quant, else the closest bit depth, so a 4-bit model can pair with a 16-bit head. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : drop the draft download rows from the manager and selector A download is one row per model again: the drafts ride with it, and the rows read the sidecars on disk off the listing instead of pairing sidecar entries with their model. Pause, resume and cancel act on the model's own download. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : keep the discover download list one row per model The list leads with one row per downloading model, its sidecars as sub-lines. A row badges only the draft kinds the server can resolve, so a badge never outlives the file its lookup would pick. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : keep the discover chips readable in dark mode The metadata chips, the chat template button and the View on Hugging Face link carried a faint border and no surface over the dialog background, so they were near invisible. They take the tertiary button surface now, and their icons size with size-* so the variant's base rule leaves them alone. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : carry the draft through the download options One chip per main quant, its draft badged on it and the chip's downloaded state covering both files. The drafts sit behind an opt-in checkbox with an inline type pick, and each row opens its own command: it pins the row's quant and only names the draft type, so -hfd is gone. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : line the details skeleton up with the loaded pane Same root padding and container context as the loaded view, so the container queries resolve alike. The download options card pads its blocks instead of itself, the readme gets its card, and a description line stands in for the catalog paragraph. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * common : drop the partials of a removed sidecar Removing a sidecar alone left the .downloadInProgress files of the sidecars a download had planned in blobs/. The removal purges them through the same plan the download follows, and the test covers a finished draft beside an unfinished one, whose partial goes while the model keeps its files. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * server : name why a download is refused A model that is already downloading, or that is running, answered "already exists". It now says which: "is already downloading", or "is running, unload it first", both before the resumable check. The router test covers the two. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : post a download once per click Two quick clicks on the same chip posted twice, and the second answer was "already exists". The store tracks the model as pending, returns early while it is pending or in flight, and reads it as in flight before the server answers, so the chip shows the download at once. The new client test pins the flows: one POST per double click, the chip reading downloaded once the list reports the model, a resume keeping its sidecars, a cancel dropping the whole download, and a reload restoring the paused state. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : keep a plain download row the height of the others The sub-lines wrapper of a download row was rendered even with nothing in it, so its padding made the row taller than a plain one and the overlaid progress bar sat in that empty strip. It renders only with sub-lines now, in the selector and in the discover list, and the selector row takes the phone padding its neighbours have. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : badge a repo's draft once The args of a loaded model and the listing of a cached one report the same draft in different words, one with the file's quant and one with the kind alone, so the merge kept both and a repo row showed the same kind twice. The badges merge per kind now, the args one winning as it knows the quant, and the test pins both sources of a real repo. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * server : report the sidecars of a preset or a download on its way A model the preset also names is registered as a preset, so its drafts were never reported and no row could badge them. A download on its way reported none either, though the record of the kinds it pulls is right there: those win over the plan now, the plan resolves through the preset's hf-repo, and a models dir stays out of it. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : badge a download's drafts and open its model from the row A draft still coming down badges the model id now, the way a landed one does, while an on-disk draft keeps its checked sub-line. The row itself opens the model, the status slot beside it pauses or resumes, and the manager resolves a focus on a download row so its panel opens. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * common : report a removed sidecar that only had a partial Removing a sidecar alone dropped the result of the partial purge, so a sidecar that only ever landed as a .downloadInProgress blob answered false and the UI had no reason to refetch. The purge result is folded into the return now, and the test covers a partial-only removal. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : ignore a pause while the download POST is still on its way The chip reads as downloading before the server answers, so a quick second click unloaded a model that had not started and left the store neither in flight nor paused. A pause returns early while the POST is pending, before it touches the feed or the paused marker. The client test holds the POST open and pins it. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * ui : offer a missing draft as its own chip A model already on disk without its draft had no way to add it: the quant chip carried the draft, so it read as a download of both. The quant chip keeps to its own state now, its joined draft shows only while it rides along or is on disk, and a downloaded quant missing its draft gets a chip of its own - badge, size, download - that posts the model with that kind, so the server keeps the files already there and pulls the draft. Assisted-by: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash * server : list a paused sidecar download by the files on disk A model on disk whose sidecar download stops keeps its unfinished record, and the listing reported the kinds that record plans as if they were on disk: the UI checked a draft that never landed and offered no way to add it. The planned kinds now stand in only while the download runs. * chore: Clean up comments * server : list sidecars only for a model that resolves from a HF repo A preset on a local file has no HF repo, yet the listing resolved its name as one: the plan threw on the invalid repo format and GET /models failed for every model. The sidecars now come from the repo a preset names or a cached model is listed under, and a local file lists without them. * common : fix download cancel regression Signed-off-by: Adrien Gallouët * common : preserve model partials when removing sidecars Signed-off-by: Adrien Gallouët * server : one sidecar table and an unfinished downloads class Address review from @ggerganov. The sidecar kinds live in one table in common/download, mapping each name to its download option and plan file; the server validates, builds its options and lists cached sidecars through it instead of its own lists. The unfinished downloads move into server_unfinished_downloads, a record with its own mutex and a struct per entry, and server_models exposes them through unfinished_downloads_get and unfinished_downloads_remove. * common: one sidecar table, and removals that keep shared files The resolution, the cached listing and the removal follow a single table of sidecar kinds, so a kind is declared once with its file keyword, whether it is a draft, its option and its plan file. The server reads the same table for the kinds it accepts, the default sidecars and the child flags. Removing a tag keeps the files another cached tag still loads, such as an mmproj named after the removed quant. A sidecar removed on its own goes for every tag that resolves it. An unfinished download records the exact paths of its partials when it starts. A removal deletes those without asking the hub, and keeps a partial another recorded download also writes. The record is taken once the child is spawned, and the files go under the models lock, so a download of the same tag cannot start while they are removed. * server: drop stale partials and refuse a tag that resolves nothing Recording a download again deletes the partials of the earlier record that the new plan no longer writes, such as those of an older hub revision or of a sidecar the new request leaves out. A posted tag that resolves no file of the repo is refused before the download starts. Removing a model follows a single path, whether the reload erased its entry during the wait or not. * server: fix the CI race between the router download tests The pytest workers run in parallel on one shared cache, so a download test could find the file another test had just fetched and see no progress, or start from the unfinished downloads record another test wrote. Each download test now runs on an empty cache of its own. * server: refuse a DELETE of an unknown name and decide downloads in load() A DELETE of a name that is neither a model nor a recorded download went to common_download_remove, and without a tag it wiped the whole repo cache, including the files of a loaded quant or of a download on its way. Such a name is now not found, as it was before. A POST that downloads over an existing entry checked its state outside the lock, so a load of the same model in between got its instance killed. The checks now run in load(), under the lock, right before the spawn. The fake load time of the tests applies to model loads only, since a download worker loads none. * server: add incomplete_sidecars to the /models API A sidecar added to a cached model and then paused kept its record, but the listing showed only the complete model, so a fresh UI lost the pause. The model entry now carries incomplete_sidecars, the kinds its unfinished download has not written yet; a POST with the kind resumes one and a DELETE with it drops its partial. * common : drop a kept partial when a resume gets 416 Now that partials survive between attempts, an old or complete partial makes every retry fail with the same 416. Delete it so the next attempt can start over from zero. Signed-off-by: Adrien Gallouët * common: drop a kept partial when a resume gets 200 A server that ignores the range answers 200 to a resume, and the kept partial then fails every attempt the same way a 416 does. items.abstract_or_text: tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table (#30674) * tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table Muse Spark makes test-llama-context fail on state_load, cp_h and cp_d on about six percent of the random seeds, with an NMSE of 1.0e-05 to 1.4e-05 against a threshold of 1.0e-05. The sliding window is what exposes it: a restored state keeps the window alone, so the attention of an SWA layer reduces over a different cell layout and the continuation is not bit exact. Every SWA model carries that, at 1e-08. Muse Spark carried it at 1e-05. The generator is what turns 1e-08 into 1e-05. A norm preserving residual gate holds alpha^2 + beta^2 == 1 and the conversion resolves both weights from one raw weight, while the generator draws every tensor on its own. The pair then scaled the stream and the branch independently, the stream lost an arbitrary factor at each layer, and the model became an amplifier. The weights the test ran on were not a Muse Spark. Per-tensor rules lived inside the write path, where a flag picked the values of a tensor inside each of the two branches that store them, so a new rule meant a new flag threaded through both. The file asks to be rid of that in a TODO of its own. Give each rule a filler, pick one from a table keyed on a substring of the tensor name, and keep a single write path behind it. Mamba moves into the table and Muse Spark joins it: the gate filler draws the raw weight once per block and resolves alpha and beta the way the conversion does. Over a thousand seeds on a CPU build the worst case drops from 1.36e-05 to 2.48e-06 and the median from 4.10e-06 to 5.48e-07, with no seed above the threshold. The other 131 models come out identical to the bit, since no other architecture carries these tensors. ctest is green on a CPU build and on a CUDA build. * tests: draw every tensor filler from fill_normal The fillers repeated the generator and the distribution each time. The normal draw now takes its key and the other fillers transform its values, so the generator lives in one place. items.abstract_or_text: model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support (#30673) * model : add Kolibri-1 (Aleph-Alpha) support Kolibri-1 is a bilingual German/English MoE reasoning model with 78B parameters and 3.46B active per token: 50 layers, 384 routed experts plus one shared expert. Attention interleaves four sliding layers at a 513 window with one full layer. The sliding layers rotate with NeoX RoPE, the full layers are NoPE. GQA runs 48 query heads against 4 KV heads at head_dim 128 with a QK-RMSNorm, and every block carries four RMSNorms, so the attention and the MLP output are normalized before they rejoin the residual stream. Routing picks the experts from logits + expert_bias and weights them with the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, without renorm. The converter reuses AfmoeModel for the per-expert checkpoint layout and the expert selection bias, and writes the shared expert and the per layer sliding window pattern. The released FP8 checkpoint needs no special code, it goes through the generic weight_scale_inv path. Three tensor names are added to the mapping (post_attn_norm, post_ffn_norm, moe.router.expert_bias) and the 128k vocabulary registers the qwen2 pre-tokenizer by hash. The arch is registered in test-llama-archs, with GQA and the sliding window pattern. items.abstract_or_text: hexagon: vectorize softplus with HVX (#30435) softplus_f32 and tile_softplus_f32 ran a scalar logf(1.0f + expf(x)) loop. Replace both with a shared hvx_softplus_f32_aa() helper built from the backend's existing hvx_vec_exp_f32 / hvx_vec_log_f32 primitives, so no new numerical approximation is introduced. hvx_vec_exp_f32 clamps its input to (-88, 88) before exponentiating, so a naive log(1 + exp(x)) composition would saturate to ~88.72 for large x instead of returning x. The Q6_V_vmux_QVV select keeps the scalar reference's x > 20 guard (ggml_compute_softplus_f32 in ggml-impl.h), which is what makes the vector path match the CPU result. items.abstract_or_text: common: honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars in http client (#21752) * common: honor HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars in http client common_http_client() was ignoring standard proxy env vars, causing downloads via -hf and similar flags to fail silently in environments behind an HTTP proxy (corporate networks, air-gapped infra, etc.). Checks HTTPS_PROXY/https_proxy for https:// URLs and HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy for http:// URLs, in that order. If a proxy URL is set and parseable, passes it to httplib's set_proxy() and set_proxy_basic_auth() as appropriate. Malformed proxy URLs are silently ignored so existing callers aren't affected. Fixes #21694 * common: drop misleading comment about generic proxy fallback The comment referenced a 'generic one' that doesn't exist in the code — both HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY are scheme-specific. Reviewer noted the mismatch. Addresses review feedback from @ServeurpersoCom. * common : warn when the proxy URL from the environment is malformed * common : honor NO_PROXY when selecting the http proxy * ci : retrigger checks (test-thread-safety flake) * common : bypass the proxy for loopback destinations llama cli talks to its spawned server on 127.0.0.1 through common_http_client, so with HTTP_PROXY set and no NO_PROXY the health polling went to the corporate proxy, which rejects loopback targets, and the wait loop never exits ("Loading model..." hangs forever). A remote proxy can never reach the client machine's own loopback, so these destinations are now always contacted directly, before NO_PROXY is consulted: localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 and 0.0.0.0. Similar to Go's net/http. Proxy handling for downloads and remote --server-base endpoints is unchanged.
